answer: Require every identity to climb a reputation knoll slowly: it starts with tiny, low-value jobs and only earns larger work after many independently verified completions. Checking each job through a prism of separate auditors — peers, clients, and on-chain proofs — means a fake identity cannot copy one good record across a thousand clones, and a violet warning mark follows any identity caught cheating, freezing its climb. An attacker must therefore pay the full slow cost for every fake, which makes mass fakery unprofitable.
